content.comment_body: Hello, Uploading on the local network works without problems. However, when attempting to use Dynamic DNS to upload the data log from outside the network, I am prompted for a password and then receive an HTTP authentication failure. I have ensured the password is correct and have even set a new password, but the issue persists. For security, external port 8000 is mapped to internal port 80. Port forwarding is also set up for 10001. The Dynamic DNS URL is: [url]:8000. Accessing the web interface through the browser allows me to log in and view the display without any issues. But when using [product_name], the authentication continually fails. Does anyone know what I might be configuring incorrectly?

Hello, Uploading a datalog file requires a [product_name] connection, even through Dynamic DNS. Some things to consider: Have you enabled remote programming (tool/transfer/remote access)? Can you upload the [product_name] program via Dynamic DNS? You might want to try using port 8080 instead of 8000. Good luck.

analysis.insight_summary: The user indicates that while data log uploads through [product_name] work locally, attempts via Dynamic DNS fail due to HTTP authentication issues, even with correct credentials. Although the external port is properly mapped and browser access works remotely, software access continues to encounter authentication errors. The user is unsure whether this stems from port settings, remote access configuration, or other factors.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects reliable data log uploading via [product_name] using Dynamic DNS, similar to their local LAN experience, and hopes authentication errors can be avoided. They also expect port and remote login configurations to function smoothly for both browser and software.
